text_fidelity_a:
Scrabble Turbo Slam My feelings about this product are mixed -- We've long been fans of Scrabble, and thought we'd shake things up a bit by trying a different variation of the game. The Electronic Turbo Slam device, first required (3)- AAA batteries (not included). The device, when slammed has pretty loud sound effects/music, which I found annoying after a short while. I also thought there was too much commotion for me with everyone trying to slap down cards to change the letters, and I wasn't crazy about making just (4) letter words. As an adult, baby boomer, I much prefer the standard game of Scrabble -- quiet, relaxed and educational, and with more word potential.

I can see that this would be a great game for parents to play with young children to help them get interested in learning new words -- I would use it as an educational tool, instead of having them feel pressured to make words at record speed.

On the other hand, the speed and noise factor, would probably appeal to lots of teens. Overall, the game is relatively inexpensive, and worth a try for families who enjoy word faster paced, action filled games.
text_fidelity_b: Scrabble Turbo Slam

text_fidelity_a:
Play-Doh 36 Can Mega Pack of Non-Toxic Modeling Compound, 3 Oz Cans I routinely play with Play-doh with the three grandkids that are 3 to 4 years old. By that age they have quit eating the stuff and aren't so old as to have lost interest.

This is the ideal sized container. The larger containers have too much doh for small hands.

This is a great set of colors. Some of the colors (like black, brown, and white) are hard to find in smaller sets.

I don't buy the sets that squish the doh into shapes. Although they tons of fun, the doh gets stuck and hardens and you end up discarding the squishers. I buy cheap sets of cookie cutters, plastic cutting boards, one large good rolling pin, and lots of devices to cut and roll (be creative).

Too keep the doh moist, occasionally add a 1/2 tsp of water to all the cans and let them set for a couple of days.
text_fidelity_b: Play-Doh 36 Can Mega Pack of Non-Toxic Modeling Compound, 3 Oz Cans

text_fidelity_a:
Chutes and Ladders Board Game Like many of us over 40, we grew up with this game and recognize the graphics of the Classic Chutes and Ladders Board Game. Recently, after my dad passed, we cleared out our old house and found my old game. It followed my brother home to his family, but now I'm curious to compare the two.

Outside of nostalgia, the question is if the game stands on its own in 2015. My four year-old boy thinks so. He doesn't care about 1972 (or even know it existed, as time began with him, as he sees it). He begs to play it, right along with Trouble! and Legos.

Essentially, there's no strategy. The person going version has a small chance of winning, but for all intents and purposes, it is pure chance.

To move forward, the player spins from 1-6. Whatever square he might land on is either neutral, a ladder or a slide. Slides move him back to an earlier square, ladders move him up, and neutral squares allow him to stay put until the next move. There is no decision making.

Is it fun? Very much so, according to my boy. As there are 100 squares, there are plenty of opportunities to climb ladders and slide down. It is a little tricky to follow which direction to go, as the numbers start left-to-right, but zig-zag at each end. A patient older child or adult needs to be on-hand to help with game play.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com
text_fidelity_b: Chutes and Ladders Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model I bought this model for my 7 year old grandson who recently started riding and currently aspires to be a Vet. The model is small and some of the bits are tiny but manageable if one has reasonable dexterity. It is not for the easily frustrated as it requires patience and a thought to put together. The documentation is marginally helpful, and we used the picture on the cover more that we did the provided sheet for guidance. I also bought "Horse Anatomy (Dover Nature Coloring Book)" which proved a useful addition.
I worked with my grandson to put the model together for the first time. One of the small pieces had molding flash still attached which prevented it from fitting properly until the excess material was removed. The pieces will all fit together properly, but the final assembly is not terribly robust.
To reiterate, it was a bit of a problem solving exercise to fit the pieces into the correct spots, but we found the feeling of accomplishment worth the effort. I do not recommend this as a quick-assembly toy. There are better choices for that purpose. However, I do recommend it as a learning exercise for the curious child. It was fun to see my grandson made associations with his dog and human anatomy during the process. The finished product is suitable for display in a safe spot and can be disassembled and reassembled as long as one keeps track of all the pieces (you wouldn't want to lose his pancreas, would you?). I deducted a star for the less than great documentation.
text_fidelity_b: Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+ We'd already bought the Sneaky Squirrel Game, which is similar to this game. We've though it was one of the cutest games ever, so we were thrilled to add this one to our collection, too!

With this game, you'll get one of the cutest boxes you've ever seen! (Let me note here that the top and bottom of the game box do NOT fit inside each other. It's the same with the squirrel game.) You'll also get a super cute pair of Shelby tweezers, 4 bowls, a packet of bones, and a double spinner.

Playing the game is pretty simple. There can be up to 4 players at a time. Each player will spin first to see if they will get bones or lose bones or just lose a turn. The second spin is to determine how many bones they will win/lose. If they land on a seagull, it means they will lose bones. If they land on the hungry pug, they get to steal bones from another player. Busy pug means they lose a turn, and landing on the bones mean they win bones for their bowl. They can pick up the bones they win/lose with the tweezers.

The tweezers are a great way to develop motor skills. The game itself is a great, fun way to learn counting skills. My 5 year old is delayed and really struggles with numbers, so I'm always thrilled to find a new, exciting way to teach them to him. This is also a fun game for my 2 year old. It IS pretty simple, so I imagine, on average, 2-4, maybe 5, is probably the best ages for this game.

Overall, this is a super cute game! I can highly recommend this AND the Sneaky Squirrel Game for your young little ones!
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+

Mattel Games Pictionary: Frame Game I was really excited about this product, as Pictionary is one of my all-time favorite party games. This was a disappointment on so many levels.

First, there is no storage box. It comes with a frame, a frame stand, a timer, and a marker. And a dice, which got lost in no time. The "frame" itself is about the size of a sheet of paper (8" by 10"), and it is clear, so you can see through it. The small size makes it ideal for travel or a backpack, but the fact that it is clear makes it difficult to see when holding it on your lap. And forget about using it on the black coffee table. It works much better when used flat, on a light background surface. I like that you can use the frame as a window, so the see-through feature may be useful one at a time. It's pretty much impossible for two people to write on opposite sides of the board at the same time. Honestly it is pretty much for anyone to write on the board when it is in the stand, which keeps the board vertical.

We like to use large dry-erase boards when we pay Pictionary. I would recommend that rather than this game. The frame might be fun to draw on once in a while -- but shy not get a small whiteboard, which is much better suited for the purpose?
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games Pictionary: Frame Game

Little Live Aqua Dragons - Deep Sea Habitat - LED Light Up Tank Hatch and Grow Aquatic Pets | Amazon Exclusive I still have fond memories of Sea Monkeys from when I was a child. It's one of those simple things that bring great joy. As far as I can tell, these are the same thing, only they're called Aqua Dragons. The aquarium is also bigger than the one I had as a child. This set comes with a pouch of eggs, a pouch of food, a spoon, a bubble creator(suction tube), a little magnifying glass, and the aquarium. The aquarium has a removable top and lights that come from the bottom. Simply press a button on the side to turn them on and press it again to turn them off. It comes with batteries, though it does say they're only temporary for the "try me" feature and should be replaced. Non-chlorinated water is recommended.

We've had great fun with our little dragons. It took close to 48 hours for us to be able to see them. Of course, at that point they're only a tiny white dot and it gets more fun when they're bigger. This set has potential to last quite awhile, too. The Aqua Dragons can live up to 6 months. After they all die, you're supposed to completely let the tank dry out. This will cause any eggs to dry out. (Don't wash it out or the eggs will be washed away. The eggs won't hatch unless they've dried out.) Once that happens, you can add more water and start with a fresh batch of little dragons.

It's a great kit to create some special childhood memories.

Note on the aquarium: Don't pull the plastic. I thought it had a protective layer and almost started peeling it off. If you do, the design on it will come off with it. I do wish the plastic was flatter against the aquarium, so it's not as big of an issue thinking it's supposed to be peeled off.
text_fidelity_b: Little Live Aqua Dragons - Deep Sea Habitat - LED Light Up Tank Hatch and Grow Aquatic Pets | Amazon Exclusive

ALEX Toys Artist Studio My Art Spinner This toy is plenty entertaining for a short while. It is great fun to make the art, and the paint colors are bright and contemporary (neon green, yellow, coral, blue, and purple). The spinner is seemingly durable, powered by one C-cell battery (which is not included).

But, consider --

The bottles of ink are teeny-weeny -- .6 fl oz each -- about the size of a small hotel shampoo bottle. The jars of glitter are even tinier. Although the kit contains glitter, there is no glue to apply it. The glitter seems like a bit of an afterthought. And for some reason, even though there are five colors of paint, spinner device contains only three holes to hold the paint.

The cards to paint on are tiny as well -- there are ten cards that are about 4"x 4" each, and another ten cards that are about 3" x 3". Half are black and half are white. You may be able to make "beautiful art" (says so right on the box) but at 3" x 3", it's hard to make much of a statement.

The kit contains a clear plastic "splash guard" That is labeled in tiny font as such, along with a "do not discard" warning. If you happened to overlook the label, you would likely discard the splash guard, as it is indistinguishable from much packaging.

I have a similar spin-art painter from Crayola, the color spinner -- hard to say which one of these two items would be preferable. This Alex spinner is battery-operated, the Crayola one is not. This Alex spinner definitely has cooler paint colors. The Crayola spinner has circular pieces of cardboard to paint on. They are much larger and the shape is more interesting. Either kit would be fun for kids. Once or twice.

This would be a fun toy to play with once or twice, but I wouldn't expect it to be something you will return to again and again. And if you purchase it, don't forget to get a C-cell battery.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Toys Artist Studio My Art Spinner

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola DigiTools Paint Pack Okay first off -- you can just download the app for this product in your Apple or Android app store. It will be somewhat limited, including having some of the "backgrounds" aka digital coloring pages disabled. There are more than one DigiTools apps - I was able to unlock two of the currently available four with this set: Their paint app and their airbrush app. Other sets that include different tools can unlock the other two (including a 3D set). The App consists of the backgrounds and several solid colored canvases. Using the appropriate tool allows you to do things like paint, stamp included images onto your scene, roll paint or images along your painting. Staying true to the Crayola kid friendly tradition the app doesn't include any sort of advanced features (no layers, etc). Your tools, an eraser, and an undo button are all you will find here.

The tools (what you're really buying here) consists of a Stamper, a roller, a brush, and an airbrush. Basically all of these (except the brush) are just several stylus nubs embedded into plastic tools that are kid friendly. The brush looks just like a run of the mill cheap brush (I can see kids grabbing it to paint with for real so look out for that) but when you hold it properly it too works like a stylus.

If you or the kids graduate out of the app and decide that say they do want to use them on more advanced programs? Good news and bad news there... The good news is that since these are basically just kid friendly tablet tools, yes these work in others apps. The bad news is that if you plan to say drag the stamper across your screen to get three lines at once? That's not going to happen. The screen will see this same as if you are using two fingers at once. So, for example, when I used these tools in Sketchbook pro? The brush worked perfectly. The airbrush and roller tools worked IF I tilted them so that only one nub was touching the screen at a time (otherwise it thought I was trying to pinch in and out / zoom). The stamper tool, which has three nubs, was basically useless.

The brush (the most useful tool in the pack) is also what makes this overall a 4 not a 5 star tool. The bristles are very fragile, I used this set a couple of times, put them away in the included carrying case, went to draw again and hmm the bristles were all fanned out and bent back. I don't know that the brush will hold up long term, it's already the most finicky tool in the set. Still, a fun kid friendly set that adults will love too.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola DigiTools Paint Pack

Bezier Games Werebeasts Ted Alspach and his Bezier Games companies bring us another small-box Werewolf themed game. This game shares a similar deception element, and artwork with previous releases, but like "Werewords", this is not a mainline Werewolf game or expansion.

In this game, players are auctioning off beasts of various types, and players are bidding on these creatures, whether they truly want them or not. This is because one major mechanic of the game is calling other players out on collecting specific types of creatures - if you are correct that they are hoarding a specific creature-type, then they are punished

Ultimately, this game did not appeal to us. It has a learning curve to playing, but once you get the hang of it, it makes the game feel a little too random. No matter what you really want, you need to either make a large number of offers, or make remarkable guesses about which goals other players have. Both are legitimate ways to win, but like a more standard "classic" board game, there is a definite strategy that you want to use, and there isn't a lot of replayability in this one for our group.

In our group, the only player who really liked it was the winner, and even she wasn't entirely sold on this one. It's fast, and simple, but it's a little too easy to make guesses on what other players want, and the artwork is strange.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Werebeasts

PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player I looked forward to playing this game, but was very disappointed. It sounds fun - each player rolls five dice and adds their roll to the roll of a common die. I thought it would be more like Yahtzee, but it was not nearly as fun as that classic game. The common die gives the chance for each player to double their score, which helps someone come from behind and catch up with the player that is leading. However, when rolling only 5 dice, the odds of getting a decent roll were slim. It was almost impossible to get anything more than a three of a kind, and that was hard to do. This made the game more frustrating than fun. I've never played the original Farkle, and we had to make some house rules because many portions of the instructions were unclear, which added to my frustration. The instructions referred to online video directions being available, but I didn't think it was worth having to watch a video to learn to play what should have been a very simple dice game.

For those familiar with Farkle, the common die may add an interesting twist, but the bubble-popper and dice risers are unnecessary. The bubble-popper for the common die does not roll the die well and seems like it would break after a few uses. We took the die out and rolled it by hand. This was much easier and kept the game moving more quickly. (On a side note, when we removed the die from the bubble-popper, it looked dirty!) The dice risers are rickety and make the play of the game more confusing. Since you can't combine the numbers you get on individual rolls, it's necessary to keep track of what you got on each roll within a round. It was impossible to do this on the risers, so we just started putting the dice aside from each roll and not using the risers at all.

The dice themselves are sturdy, even though the white coloring started coming off the numbers after only a couple of uses. I like that there are four sets in different colors so each player can have their own color. However, the red and orange were too similar in color and it was hard to tell them apart.

Overall, I think the dice risers and bubble-popper are flimsy and just a gimmick to make more out of the game than there is. It's not an exciting game and became very boring when it became clear it was too hard to get a decent score from an individual roll.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player

text_fidelity_a:
VTech Sit-to-Stand Alphabet Train I don't know about a kid being strangled by the alphabet train. I suppose it's possible as there is a dip in between the two pieces of the train. My problems, however, are just of a different nature. I think this may be one of the most poorly designed toys I've ever purchased for my toddler..
I bought the train on a whim because it was on sale. It's colorful, makes noise, blah blah blah. After a couple of weeks of use, I started to notice the flaws in the design of the toy, and you know it seems like VTech has a bad habit of just putting out colorful, noisy crap that they know parents will buy regardless if it's good quality and design or not.
First of all, the thing is LOUD. There are two "choices" for volume, but the one that's supposed to be quieter can be heard across our 2500 square foot house. This is a common toy problem; I believe that the idiots coming up with kids' toys do not actually HAVE children, or they would put a quieter setting on these toys so that parents aren't stuck in the "LET'S RIDE THE ALPHABET TRAIN!" hell day after day.
Second, the train is too freaking narrow. It's too easy to topple over, so when my still-a-bit-unsteady 14-month-old would try to get on it to "ride", he often fell over. Now he's a lot better with balance at 18 months, but the thing is still too narrow.
Third, the train is not designed well for riding at all. Yes, it has handles and a seat, but the design of them is pretty unusable until the kid is way too old to be playing with an alphabet train. I watched my toddler today try to get on the toy and ride it; where his little butt goes is where the hump in the train car is, and if he sat back far enough to get off the hump, he couldn't reach the handles. What the crap? My child is not a chimp and he's not Stretch Armstrong. Why are the engine and car so far apart?
Ugh. We're keeping the dang thing because he does like to put the blocks into the train and watch them shoot out the engine. But as far as usability, the alphabet recognition is really the only thing that the toy has accomplished. If I could go back in time, I'd never buy this stupid train.
text_fidelity_b: VTech Sit-to-Stand Alphabet Train

Hot Spot is a fire truck with a really long crane on his hand that you're not supposed to be able to take off, making him awkward to pose as a robot. Once you get him into robot mode, which is no easy feat, you'll have a heck of a time getting him back into firetruck mode. Even once he's there, you can clearly see his robot hands on the top of the truck, and his legs (which form the bottom of the truck and include the back wheels), will consistently half-transform while trying to wheel him around on the ground.

All this and Hotspot is the better half of the duo. Blades, the helicopter, looks like an awkward chicken when transformed into robot mode, which is not helped by the fact that he appears to not have any hands or arms. The instructions for transforming him were incredibly difficult to decipher, as they have frequent close ups of pieces which I can't really find on my model and curvy arrows pointing at different spots. If a 31 year old with a master's degree can't figure him out, how do we expect a 6-year-old with limited patience to do it?

text_fidelity_a:
The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe) The resistance is a fantastic game with a great price and superb components. The rules are very simple also so the game can be picked up by nearly anyone in a matter of minutes. A sample round will remove any doubt about the rules and is often the best way I have found to teach the game.

So what is this about? The Resistance is a game of guessing and deduction that is rules light and fun heavy. In the basic game 5 to 10 players take on the role of either good guys or bad guys by being dealt cards that depict their character. Good guys or the resistance are blue and spies are red. The ratio of spies to resistance is driven by the number of players in a game. The spies always have fewer allies in the game than do the resistance players.

Once the players have secretly looked at their role card, everyone closes their eyes. The first player commands everyone to close their eyes, he then commands the spies and only the spies to open their eyes and look around to identify each other, he then commands them to close their eyes and lastly commands everyone to open their eyes.

So now the spies know who each other are but the allies have no idea.

The game is then played as 5 simple 'missions'. A mission consists of the first player choosing a number
of players to 'go on the mission'. The number is dependent on how many total players are playing. The more players, the more involved in each mission. Each mission from 1 to 5 will have gradually more players involved.

Everyone votes to allow or disallow the chosen players to go on the mission. Each player will have two cards to vote
with each round. These cards are marked clearly with symbols to indicate if you do or do not agree to allow the chosen players to play.

Here is where the game gets going. If the vote fails to allow the chosen players to go on the mission twice in a row, the spies win automatically.

If the players allow the mission to go forward, those players involved get to either make the mission successful or to sabotage the mission. This is done my dealing each player involved in the mission two cards. One of each success and sabotage. They secretly place their cards into two piles. The mission result and the dead pile.

Spies can sabotage or succeed a mission and the resistance players MUST succeed the mission.

The majority of succeed of sabotage rules the mission.

Rounds continue like this until the spies or the resistance have a best 3 out of 5 missions won by their side.

Up until this point your first game might seem kinda boring. But just wait, almost immediately you will figure
out who your junior sleuths are! Finger pointing and accusations will begin to fly out of the most timid players
mouths!

You will find players who are just 100% certain they know who is who and are almost always wrong! You will find out that some of your friends are REALLY GREAT LIARS and some are REALLY POOR LIARS!

The compound the fun there is also a plot deck. The plot deck is simply a deck of cards that each round, one is dealt by the first player and he can give it to someone else or keep it.
These cards are things like 'look at someone else role card' or 'veto a vote'.

I initially thought the plot deck would be horrible but I was very wrong. The first time we pulled a card that let one player look at another players role card the player looked and claimed the other player was a spy. The player accused immediately did a double take and denied the allegation fervently!

We were back at square one but now had two more people we couldn't trust! FUN! FUN! FUN!

You cannot go wrong with this game unless you live in a convent full of people with ZERO personality who have had all their fun genes removed.

So if you are looking for an excellent game, with super components, short playing time, and an immeasurable amount of fun, look no further than this gem!
text_fidelity_b: The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe)

Games The Original Tiny Hands Challenge Games- Tiny Hands Challenge Children's Toy has all the things that make for a great game- it’s challenging, fun, moves fast and has plenty of hilarious laughter. The game comes with: 2 tiny hands, 2 tinier hands, 3 sets of activity cards (151 total), 20 scoring tokens, 1 spinner, 1 string (shoe lace), 1 ball, 1 sand timer (time is one minute), 1 wager mat and instructions. You can play with 4-10 players and recommended age is 8 and up.

You begin by dividing into 2 teams- yellow and blue. You set up the wager mat and the 3 decks of cards. Then set out the hands, spinner, string, ball and sand timer. You play rock, paper, scissors to see who goes first. You spin the spinner to see which activity card you will do and which hands you will do it with- tiny or tinier. Some of the activities use pens, paper, cups and coins, so you will want to have these items available too.

Once you know what activity you must do with which hands, you make a wager. If you lose, your opponent gets the token points. Even if you win, your opponent can challenge you. The 3 sets of cards are: Solo, Pair and Charades. The timer being one minute long makes the challenges and charades almost impossible to finish in such a short time. Luckily, some of the challenges don’t use the timer and give you multiple tries. There is also a Face Off, where both teams do a challenge at the same time. Doing the challenges and charades in such a short time with these tiny hands is almost impossible and laughing so hard totally impossible. The first team to collect 31 token points wins. Great Fun, Challenges and Laughter. 5 STARS.
text_fidelity_b: Games The Original Tiny Hands Challenge

It comes with 2 little magnetized genies. There's also a magnetized chair included, so that the non-magnetized genies(sold separately) can work with this set, too. When the lever is pulled, it will move the magnet inside the toy, causing the genies to "float". Best of all, no batteries are needed!

You can buy other genies to go with this set, and there are little pegs all around to hold them. The included two work perfectly fine with this set, though, and those pegs can just be used to move around those two. You don't have to buy more, but you have that option.

Crayola Presharpened Number 2 Pencil Classpack, School Supplies, 12 Count, 144 Pack Kids love color, and these pencils with their jazzy, colorful erasers are sure to please. What a great idea instead of the boring brown erasers.

As a teacher, I've spent many hours sharpening pencils for my kindergarten, first grade and elementary students. I didn't want to use class time for them to sharpen pencils.

So, having these pre-sharpened pencils is a great way to start the year.

They are very comfortable to hold, as they don't have the ridges. They are nice and smooth. They feel good in your hands.

The points are very sharp, but don't break easily.

I thought the lead seemed lighter in color than other #2 pencils I've used on my printer paper, but when I used it in my planner it looked like regular #2 lead, so it was probably the paper. If you press down harder, then the color of the lead on the paper looks the same.

It says no latex in eraser. The erasers work better on these pencils than standard pencils which I've used. So, I guess the no latex feature helps.

I find these pencils as good as, or superior, to others I have used.

There would make a great gift for a teacher so she doesn't have to buy pencils out of her personal funds. Or a teacher could give a box to each student at the beginning of the year.

I like the weight and feel of these pencils.

The box which these pencil boxes come in is sturdy, and would fit well in a closet with shelves for storage for the school year.

Colorforms 70th Anniversary Set - The Classic Picture Toy That Sticks Like Magic - Ages 3+ I'm in my 60's and remember Colorforms from when I was a kid. It was and still is in my opinion one of the greatest toys around. Shapes are placed onto a background board and they cling to the board, so the possibilities of creating designs and story scenes are endless.

I do a lot of geometric designing so have a reproduction of the original set, and this anniversary set makes a great addition. The original set is all basic single color shapes. These anniversary sheets (consisting of 4 separate unbound sheets) have those same shapes plus more, and some of these have multiple colors in one shape, with some of those colors being in different patterns and shades as opposed to being all solid colors. There ARE some solid colors, but there are also patterns with stripes, dots, triangles, circles inside of circles, half moons, etc. So this set expands on the designing possibilities with the added dimensions of patterns and color shades. As with the original set, these shapes are peeled off the page they come on and are then placed onto a black background sheet (included) which they cling to until removed.

These sheets are smaller than the original set that comes in a plastic spiral bound book. So if you already have the original in its box, you can just take these sheets from this anniversary set and store in with the original if you don't want to store 2 separate boxes. Overall a nice set that is great as an artsy and learning tool for kids and designing tool for adults who enjoy working with geometric shapes.
text_fidelity_b: Colorforms 70th Anniversary Set - The Classic Picture Toy That Sticks Like Magic - Ages 3+

Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud This is a completely different kind of game and the idea of stars and lanterns is abstract. It says it is easy to learn, but to be honest, don't bring your friends together to learn the game. You should set it up, read through the directions and pretend to have two friends with you to understand what is going on. THEN you can explain the game to your friends. The reason is because you can tell this game was not designed in America, there are a few minor English mistakes. The directions have interesting choice of words. So I'm going to try my best by using parentheses to show the words they used in the directions.

The goal of the game is when a word card is revealed, you try to figure out which dixit (picture) cards match that word--by the picture itself, the color(s), inspiration, characters, etc. Then you mark an X (cross) for each dixit card you feel matches that word. At the same time, you want to choose cards you think your friends will choose. If your friends chose that card too, both of you earn stars (sparks) and so on. If they didn't, then you lose (fall) and stop there. If you marked X for too many dixit cards (hoping to get a lot of points), more likely your friends won't have that same card marked and that will make you lose. You have to work like a team, trying to figure out what your friends will choose and win. (This is what they mean by the word, greedy.) This is a good way to teach kids how to perceive the pictures and THINK of others and what they could be thinking, again a "teamwork." This is where it is supposed to be fun. My daughter liked it, but my son didn't like it.

I have one suggestion for you as parents or caregiver of a child age 8 or over. (Ages for the game is for 8+.) I suggest you form the first few turns, you handpick the words you feel your child will be able to "match" then go from there. You handpicking and seeing a few cards in advance honestly does not change the game. The game actually entirely relies on the other players' dixit card choices.

There is one rule that seems pointless. Of course you need to read the directions first to understand what I"m talking about. Here I go anyway--suppose you "fall" then at the end of the game when everyone is ready to score. If you have some sparks and a super-spark from one of your dixit cards that you marked off (crosses), you wipe away one star (but not the super-spark star) then count the remaining stars (sparks). The super-spark star has the same point value as the other sparks so I'm not sure why it makes a difference to wipe off a star or a super-spark star.

This game is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. It's also created in China and I don't know that it's going to be that great, at least for some U.S. audiences.
text_fidelity_b: Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud

text_fidelity_a:
Mega Bloks TMNT Collectors Krang's Rampage Building Kit We're huge Lego fans in my house, so while it may not be fair, I couldn't help but compare Mega Bloks with Lego. We got a few kits to try out, but otherwise, we've only used Lego in the past(though quite a bit of it). Unfortunately, Mega Bloks has just fallen short, for me, and I wasn't overly impressed(for the most part).

First of all, I've been spoiled to numbered bags. While this kit is divided into separate bags, you have to open all of them and dump them out, because the pieces you need for each step could be in any of the bags. I prefer, if I'm using a kit, to have my steps divided by bags. It keeps thing from getting less jumbled and lost, and it provides great "rest" points. It kind of made me wonder what the point of all the bags were in this set.

Second, these blocks just didn't go together smoothly. Some of them require a great deal of pressure to get attached. They hurt my fingers. I even snapped my finger between two of the blocks at one point trying to get pieces together. (Sad, but true.) My fingers just ache after working with Mega Blocks due to the amount of pressure required to get some of the pieces together. Some of the pieces were incredibly frustrating to get together. Not only that but some of the parts from the final product keep falling off/apart. It took so long to put the thing together(with so much pain) that it almost brings some tears to see parts fall off. ;)

Third, the directions aren't as clear as I'd prefer. Sure, as an adult, I figured things out, but for the average child, the directions just make things harder than they have to be.

When I discovered that Mega Bloks were compatible with Lego, I was really excited. I thought that the block building world could open up to more options for me and my children. We're sticking with Lego, though! It seems more organized and the pieces are more reliable. (They have more of a perfect fit than we've experienced with Mega Bloks.)

In defense of Mega Bloks, though, the little figurines are way cooler, and they have soft parts! IF you are a fan of Mega Bloks, this kit is cool! (I just found it a pain. Literally.)
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks TMNT Collectors Krang's Rampage Building Kit

text_fidelity_a:
World Series of Yahtzee Board Games [[VIDEOID:9706f008dc0f922f2a22889963de0e00]] This is a digital, board-based game of Yahtzee. I think it's made to compete with [[ASIN:B0042ET8S0 Uno Attack Game]] and [[ASIN:B001G5431A Bunco]], and it is much more fun than both of those games. Sometimes making a classic into a digital version is a mistake, but the designers did an awesome job with this game.

It's still [[ASIN:B00000IWH6 Yahtzee]]. You still get five dice, and you have to match the classic Yahtzee combinations of Yahtzee (five of a kind), four of a kind, three of a kind, full house, small straight (sequence or run) and large straight. But, everybody plays at once with their own sets of five dice, and the computer in the middle moderates everything, so goes very quickly and it's exciting.

The little buzzer in the middle is pretty sophisticated for a simple computer. It records who buzzes in and in which order you buzzed in, and it plays some fun countdown music. You get five seconds after the first person finishes to finish rolling and to buzz in yourself. Each person can collect up to one card per turn, based on what they rolled, but if you're not lucky, or if someone else gets your combination first, then you don't get any cards per turn. Usually turns take about thirty seconds each, and a full game all the way through will take about ten minutes, so it's very fast paced and fun.

I really liked the original Yahtzee, and I really like this too.

Pros:
+Very fun new version of an already fun classic
+Doesn't waste paper like the old version
+No more waiting around for slow players, like the old version
+You really should start playing this instead of Bunco, since there's a lot more strategy in this game
+You can roll the dice as many times as you want, where in traditional Yahtzee, you could only roll the dice three times per turn

Cons:
-The black dice with the red dots are so much cooler than the rest of the dice, so everyone will be fighting over these
-Made out of cheap plastic cardboard. If you love this game, which you probably will, and if you're not a dainty family, which you probably aren't, then you'll break these pretty quickly and go through about one of these games per year. It's still cheaper than a night at the movies, though, and this game is fun enough to justify getting a new one.
text_fidelity_b: World Series of Yahtzee Board Games

Takenoko Board Game | Bamboo Farming Game | Panda Themed Strategy Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 8+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Matagot We had the pleasure of playing this in our most recent game night, and it was delightful. You start with a few "quests" based on bamboo for pandas to eat, bamboo in the "fields", and the arrangement of those "field" tiles (as well as access to water ...). It's actually rather simple. Each turn you get to expand the game by adding field tiles (up adding water or other upgrades to the tiles), grow bamboo, have the panda eat the bamboo, or take on more "quests". As everything but the bamboo the panda eats belongs to everyone, there's a passive cooperation, and other than the score at the end (based on completing those cards), it doesn't feel that competitive. If another player lays down irrigation, that's not irrigation that solely benefits them or takes away from what you have, rather it adds to what you have and may well help complete one of your quests. We played with folks from 7 years old on up, and everyone had a great time.

The only real negative (and I don't see the need to deduct any stars from the rating) is that this is at max a four player game. I could'd imagine playing with less than 3, and 4 really is the sweet spot.
text_fidelity_b: Takenoko Board Game | Bamboo Farming Game | Panda Themed Strategy Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 8+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Matagot
